study: Wolf et al. 2018, ELLA-V (English Language and Literacy Acquisition-Validation) ESL curricula + virtual mentoring/coaching, i3 RCT, Texas (eval by CRRE Johns Hopkins)
eval_evidence: The Center for Research and Reform in Education (CRRE) at Johns Hopkins University 'were contracted to conduct the independent evaluation'; CRRE also did the random assignment. The ELLA-V program was developed by Texas A&M researchers, a separate party.
developer_evidence: PD and coaching were 'provided by Texas A&M University' — the program developers (professors/researchers at Texas A&M who created the ELLA-V curricula and the Virtual Professional Development / Virtual Mentoring and Coaching) delivered the supports to teachers.
cascade_evidence: Texas A&M (developer) coaches/PD providers delivered training and virtual coaching directly to the treatment teachers; no train-the-trainer / lead-teacher intermediary described.
counterfactual_evidence: Both treatment arms (T1, T2) were compared against a common Business-as-Usual control; BAU teachers continued their usual ESL/literacy instruction with no ELLA-V curricula, PD, or coaching.
coaching_evidence: Virtual Mentoring and Coaching gave teachers 'up to three rounds of lesson feedback' per year (Jan-May) via field notes/observation records — a few periodic coaching/observation cycles, light rather than recurring monthly/biweekly in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: ELLA-V is a set of teacher-delivered ESL/literacy curricula replacing/augmenting regular instruction; the intervention changes the teacher's classroom instruction, with no separate tutoring, pull-out, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Backwards grade rollout (one grade per year); teachers and students were exposed for a single school year per cohort/grade, each measured at the end of that one year — a single-year exposure design with no prior-implementation maturity wave.
